The point $P(\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{3},\frac{1}{3})$ lies on the unit circle, as shown. What is $\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta ?$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14222207/assets/df5d54940a136a53c1e1c00f8cc9d71d7b064f6e0895a029da2738cf21998a56.png)

Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta $ as follows:

$$
x=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta 
$$

We're given that $x=\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}$ and $y=\frac{1}{3}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{3},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{3}.
$$

Knowing that $\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta },$ we can calculate $\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta :$

$$
\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta =\frac{(\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{3})}{(\frac{1}{3})}=2\sqrt{2}.
$$
